scope: full ten-prompt GGUF AR/MTP suite plus transition-normalized llama.cpp HIP diagnostic

hardware.device: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S Graphics

model.quant: UD-Q4_K_M GGUF with one embedded MTP block

timing_contract.hipengine_true_ar: first token from prefill and one warmup token excluded; host wall begins before the first of N measured session.step calls and ends after the Nth returns
timing_contract.hipengine_mtp_canonical: visible output tokens divided by summed draft plus target stage wall; retained for same-harness MTP/AR history
timing_contract.hipengine_mtp_cross_engine: visible output tokens divided by complete cycle_wall_ms from proposal-cycle entry through target verification, state commit, acceptance, and output accounting
timing_contract.llamacpp_native: predicted_n divided by predicted_ms; not cross-engine comparable because t_start_generation is set after the first output token is sampled while predicted_n includes it
timing_contract.llamacpp_cross_engine: request N+1 outputs and divide sum(predicted_n - 1) by sum(predicted_ms); N=24 timed transitions per prompt in this refresh
timing_contract.client_wall: includes prompt processing, HTTP, and response handling and is reported only as a separate diagnostic

cross_engine_comparison.qualification: decode-only transition wall; different bf16 versus f16 KV types remain disclosed; client/end-to-end request wall is not compared

conclusions: Current exact/default B5 is 51.813 versus 54.137 true-AR tok/s (0.9571x), so exact MTP no longer wins on gfx1151.
Explicit llama-compat B2 remains a full-suite win at 69.496 versus 54.397 true-AR tok/s (1.2776x); every category and heldout beat true AR.

The prior exact 61.979 tok/s row is historical: current exact cycle wall is 19.360 versus 16.162 ms/output, with replay/commit growing from 0.019 to 2.766 ms/output after the correctness/lifecycle pass.
For cross-engine decode boundaries, hipEngine llama-compat is 69.382 tok/s and llama.cpp is 66.660 tok/s over exactly 24 timed transitions per prompt.
llama.cpp native predicted_per_second is retained only as native reporting because it counts the prompt-produced first output token outside predicted_ms.
llama-compat remains explicit-only and accuracy-traded despite its speed because it is not serial-prefix-equivalent.
